correctness.rationale: The derivative-measure representation and Minkowski identify the seminorm-to-norm constant with a single-step-function supremum; continuity in its jump position attains it for finite p, away from the two constant end steps. In the Durrmeyer beta mixture, conditional variance contributes another x(1−x)/n to the binomial variance; the gamma representation and the delta method have centered Gaussian limits along every interior sequence of starts. Conditioning characteristic functions for the fixed r successive increments adds their Gaussian variances, since the intervening states converge to the same interior limit and the conditional limits are uniform for starts converging to it. Chebyshev gives an integrable |z|⁻² majorant away from the center in the rescaled crossing profile. The endpoint crossing estimate integrates to O(sqrt(t(1−t)/n+n⁻²)+(1+log(n+1))/n); neither endpoint can compete at the n⁻¹/² scale of the pth power. The moving-center limit is therefore maximized uniquely at 1/2, and compactness gives the strict relative gap outside any fixed midpoint neighborhood. Minkowski then forces any near-optimal input to have vanishing relative variation outside that neighborhood. For L∞, continuity in the start gives an essential lower bound by the smoothed jump evaluated at zero (take x→0 with x<t); this tends to 1 as t↓0 by atomlessness. The matching upper bound is by positivity and constant reproduction. The two degree-two, two-iterate squared L² midpoint examples were independently checked by integrating affine residuals.
residual_risks: Fixed p and r; no uniformity as either grows. The finite examples are not a proof of the asymptotic or of finite-degree maximizing locations.

value.rationale: The uniform worst-case comparison of two canonical approximants distinguishes their smoothing penalty by an exact factor 2^(1/(2p)) and calibrates repeated smoothing by r^(1/(2p)). The strict away-from-center gap describes where any nearly worst discontinuous datum must place its variation; this is useful beyond estimating a test jump. The L∞ obstruction separates uniform-norm approximation from finite-p decay.
residual_risks: No exact optimizer geometry at every degree, growth regime in r or p, or robustness claim for other kernels is established.
